the numerical analysis on the instability behavior of liquid/dense films under supercritical conditions.

the numerical code developed for the present study is capable to deal with the compressible fluid flows under supercritical conditions and can be applied to the instability analysis of liquid/dense film flows.
the liquid films of the liquefying hybrid rocket fuels are unstable under the supercritical conditions and the instability is enhanced by the acceleration body force and high Reynolds number.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a new method to simulate the flow of a liquid/dense fluid layer under supercritical conditions and have obtained the instability mechanism of liquid/dense film flows in hybrid rocket engines.
the instability analysis for the liquid/dense fluid film under supercritical operating condition has been conducted and the entrainment phenomena of liquid fuel have been revealed.

the instability phenomena of dense fluid layers in a hybrid rocket chamber under supercritical conditions can be predicted by our analysis, and the entrainment of dense fluid is expected in the actual engine.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the entrainment phenomena can be suppressed by reducing the Reynolds number of the flow and by increasing the chamber pressure.
the instability analysis of liquid/dense films under supercritical conditions is a useful tool to investigate the entrainment phenomena and to design hybrid rocket engines.
a liquid film in a hybrid rocket engine is unstable, and this instability can lead to a large amount of entrainment of liquid fuel into the dense fluid layer and the combustion chamber.
